title: The Order Website
topic: Python for the web: Flask routes
briefing: Floor 6: Shipping & Orders! ByteWorks makes great computers, but nobody can buy them because we don't have a website. Let's build one with Flask. Each page is just a Python function, and a route tells Flask which web address runs which function.
hints: @app.route("/") goes on the line above a function, and whatever the function returns is the page. Put a variable part in the address with <name>, and Flask passes it into the function as a parameter.
Return a tuple to send a different status code: return "Not found", 404. For the stock page, check whether part is in stock (the dict you're given).

@app.route("/") def home(): return "

ByteWorks Shop

" / @app.route("/about") def about(): return "Hand-built computers since Day 1" / @app.route("/stock/") def stock_page(part): if part in stock: return f"{part}: {stock[part]} in stock", otherwise return f"We don't sell {part}", 404
bonus:
Add a /hello/ route that uses render_template_string("

Hi {{ name }}!

", name=name) to fill in a template.
